 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao

Judgement:
The appellant is the third respondent in M.V.O.P.No.1074 of 2007 on the file of the Motor Accident
Claims Tribunal-cum-V Additional District Judge (Ftc), Guntur and the respondents are the
petitioner and respondents 1, 2, 4 and 5 in the said case.
2. Both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in claim application.

3. The claimant filed a Claim Petition under sections 163(A) and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act against the respondents by praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- towards compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 04.06.2007.

4. The case of the claimant is that on 04.06.2007 at about 2.30 p.m. while the petitioner was travelling in an auto bearing No.AP 07 TT 5674 and when the auto reached near poultry farm at Vemuru village, the driver of auto bearing No.AP 7V 9755 drove the same in VGKRJ MACMA 1958 of 2014 a rash and negligent manner and dashed against auto, in which the petitioner was travelling,
resulting which, the petitioner sustained grievous crush injury on his right leg and the petitioner claimed an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- towards compensation for the injuries sustained by him.
5.
The first respondent remained exparte.

The respondents 2, 3 and 5 filed counters by denying the claim application and contended that the claimant is not entitled any compensation and the respondents 2, 3 and 5 are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i. Whether the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto bearing No.AP 7V 9755 or by the driver of the auto bearing No.AP 07 TT 5674?
ii. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation and if so to what amount and against whom?
iii.
To what relief?

sentences.text: 1 7. On behalf of the petitioner, PW1 and PW2 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A4 and Ex.X1 and Ex.X2 were marked.
On behalf of respondents, RW1 and RW2 were examined and Ex.B1 and Ex.B2 and Ex.X3 were marked.

8. After considering the evidence on record, the Tribunal has given a finding that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of auto bearing No.AP 7V 9755 and the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.5,10,800/- to the claimant towards compensation.
9.
Aggrieved by the same, the third respondent/ Insurance company filed the present appeal.

10. Now, the point for consideration is:
 Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any  interference?

11. POINT:-
The case of the petitioner is that he is a coolie and getting income of Rs.60/- or Rs.70/- per day for eking his livelihood.

On 04.06.2007 at about 2.30 p.m. while the petitioner was travelling in VGKRJ MACMA 1958 of 2014 an auto bearing No.AP 07 TT 5674 and when the auto reached near poultry farm at Vemuru village, the driver of auto bearing No.AP 7V 9755 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the auto, in which the petitioner was travelling, resulting which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Tenali and his right leg was amputated.
12. It is settled principle of law that in any claim petition under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, the petitioner need not prove the rash and negligent driving of the crime vehicle.
Here the claim application is filed under Section 163-A and 140 of Motor Vehicle Act.

There is evidence on record, as per Ex.A1 certified copy of First Information Report and Ex.A2 certified copy of charge sheet, the auto of first respondent was involved in the accident and charge sheet was also filed against the driver of the auto of first respondent bearing No.AP 7V 9755.
Therefore, the petitioner need not prove the rash and negligent driving of the crime vehicle.
As per the evidence on record, the petitioner filed petition under Section 163-A and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act and the petitioner also received an amount of Rs.25,000/- under no fault liability.

Therefore, in view of VGKRJ MACMA 1958 of 2014 the Judgment of Division Bench of this Court in New India Insurance Company Limited Vs. B.Malla Reddy and others1, the owner and driver of the vehicle in which the petitioner was travelling cannot be held liable to pay the compensation and the accident was occurred not due to negligence of the driver of the auto bearing No.AP 07 TT 5674 in which the petitioner was travelling, charge sheet was also filed against the driver of The United India Insurance Co. 13. RW1, who is working in a third respondent Insurance company deposed in his evidence that at the time of accident, the driver of the auto bearing No.AP 7V 9755 possessed driving licence of Auto rickshaw non-transport and the crime vehicle is auto rickshaw transport and the Insurance Company also examined the clerk in RTA office as RW2.
As per the evidence of RW2, the crime vehicle is an auto rickshaw transport and the driver of the auto rickshaw possessed non-transport only.
2002(6) ALD 137 VGKRJ MACMA 1958 of 2014 14.

In a decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental insurance Company Limited2 held that 'Light Motor Vehicle' as defined in Section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in Section 2(21) read with section 2(15) and 2(48).

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental insurance Company Limited2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such transport vehicles are not exclude from the definition of the light motor vehicle by virtue of Amended Act No.54/1994.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India further held that:
The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act.54/1994 w.e.f., 14-11-1994 while substituting classes (e) to (h) of Section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle" in section 10(2)(e), medium passenger motor vehicle in section 10(2)(f) ,
heavy goods vehicle in section 10(2)(h) with expression 'transport vehicle' as substituted in section 10(2)(e) related only to the afore said substituted classes only.
It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of section 10(20)(e) and section 2(41) of the Act i.e., light motor vehicle.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India further held that:
The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle" continuous to be the same as it was and has been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle or such class without any endorsement to that effect."
Therefore, in view of the above decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, the driving licence of driver of 1st 2017 SAR (Civil) 1008 VGKRJ MACMA 1958 of 2014 respondent is sufficient to drive the crime vehicle/auto.
Therefore, objection taken by the 3rd respondent/ Insurance Company cannot be accepted.

15. Here with regard to the transport and non-transport driving licence, the Government of India addressed a letter to all the Principal Secretaries and DGP's of all the State Governments vide letter The United India Insurance Co. Ltd. ... vs Ganisipudi Nageswara Rao, Guntur ...

In the said letter, the Government of India clearly stated that in compliance of the judgment dated 03.07.2017 of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal No.5826 of 2011 in Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited:
In view of the legal position as settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above Judgment, the requirement under Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 to obtain the transport licence would arise in case of medium/ heavy goods and passenger vehicles only.

sentences.text: No other vehicle will require any separate endorsement, even if they are used for commercial purposes.

The exemption from the requirement to obtain the endorsement for commercial vehicles would apply to following vehicles:
 i. Motor cycle without gear  ii. Motor cycle with gear iii.
Light Motor
Vehicle (goods/ passenger) iv. e-rickshaw/ e-cart VGKRJ MACMA 1958 of 2014
Therefore, in view of the above reasons, the driver of first respondent is having valid and effective driving licence to drive the crime vehicle/ auto on the date of accident.
16. The claim petitioner also examined the doctor, who treated him as PW2.
His evidence clearly goes to show that because of the accident, the claimant sustained disability of 80%.
PW2 also stated that the claimant received fracture injuries and his knee was amputated upto the right lower limb.
Ex .A3
was issued by the doctor, who treated the patient in the casualty.
PW2 further deposed that he treated the petitioner and amputation was done to avoid further complications, since the injury was above the right knee.
Therefore, the evidence of PW2 clearly shows that the claimant suffered severe mental agony and also sustained 80% disability.
In view of the grievous injury sustained by the claimant an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded and an amount of Rs.2,000/- is awarded to the claimant for one simple injury.

Since the petitioner sustained severe grievous injuries and his leg was also amputated and he suffered severe pain and suffering, an amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering and an amount of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards VGKRJ MACMA 1958 of 2014 transportation charges and an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards nutrition of food and attendant charges.
Here Ex.A3 certified copy of wound certificate and Ex.X1 case sheet show that the injured is aged about 50 years, but unfortunately the Tribunal applied the multiplier of 16.

In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Sarla Verma and another Vs. Delhi Road Transport Corporation and others 3 case, the multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased is '13'.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and another Vs. Delhi Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As per the own case of the petitioner, he was getting income of Rs.60/- or Rs.70/-
per day by doing coolie works.
Therefore, monthly income of petitioner is Rs.1800/- and annual income is Rs.21,600/-.
Accordingly the claimant is entitled an amount of Rs.2,24,640/- (Rs.21,600 x 80/100 = 17,280 x 13 = 2,24,640/-) towards 80% disability sustained by him.
Therefore, in view of the above reasons, the claimant is entitled an amount of Rs.3,01,640/- from the respondents 1 to 3.
Therefore, with the above observations, the appeal is allowed in part and the claimant is entitled an amount of Rs.3,01,640/- instead of Rs.5,10,800/- from the respondents 1 to 3.

As neither parties have placed any evidence to show their ownership of the vehicle, the responsibility of paying the claim is fixed on respondents 1 and 2 also, and no appeal is filed by the respondents 1 and 2 against the said finding.

Therefore,
respondents 1 to 3 are jointly liable to pay the said compensation.

18. In the result, this appeal is allowed in-part, by modifying the order dated 14.05.2010 passed in M.V.O.P.No.1074 of 2007 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-V Additional District Judge (FTC), Guntur.

instead of Rs.5,10,800/- from the respondents 1 to 3 with interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition, till the date of payment.
The respondents 1 to 3 are directed to deposit the said amount within one month from the date of this VGKRJ MACMA 1958 of 2014 judgment.

On such deposit,
the claimant is entitled to withdraw the same along with accrued interest thereon.

Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
